data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol collapses the workspace into the transaction log by making evidence completion and durability recording a single atomic operation on a shared substrate, rendering reclamation a cache eviction that cannot silently displace evidence because evidence never resided exclusively in the workspace.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The transactional substrate garbage-collects or compacts old seals","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Transaction logs are not efficiently queryable by problem ID","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Two-phase commit hangs and blocks reclamation indefinitely","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The workspace is mistakenly treated as authoritative rather than cache","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The deterministic per-problem workspace is treated as a pure cache; the source of truth is a transactional seal store. A process 'completes' evidence by committing a transaction containing (problem_id, content_hash, workspace_nonce). Reclamation is simply 'reclaim the cache line' and requires no additional local durable record because displacement is impossible\u2014the workspace holds only ephemeral state. What must be durably recorded is: the problem-workspace mapping, the sealed evidence hash, and the transaction commit timestamp. This adjudicates rival protocols by showing that log-based designs subsume workspace management entirely, while lease-based designs erroneously grant the workspace standalone authority.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
